🌌 NEBULA GRAPH CONTRACT v0.1 (Absorb → Graph IR)

0. Core Principle

Absorb IR is not the graph.

Absorb IR is a construction proposal for a graph.

Nebula is the authoritative store of:

  • nodes (entities)

  • edges (relations)

  • hyper-structures (clusters → subgraphs)

  • provenance (what created what)

Everything else is projection.

1. GRAPH MODEL (CANONICAL)

We define a strict typed property graph:

(Node) ---[Edge]---> (Node)
   |                   |
 properties         properties

1.1 Node Schema

JSON
{
  "node_id": "uuid",

  "type": "entity | concept | system | artifact | cluster | event",

  "label": "string",

  "properties": {
    "confidence": 0.0,
    "source_system": "absorb | voyager | external",
    "created_at": "timestamp",

    "aliases": [],
    "tags": []
  },

  "provenance": {
    "created_by": "absorb_run_id",
    "derived_from": ["signal_id | entity_id"]
  }
}

1.2 Edge Schema

JSON
{
  "edge_id": "uuid",

  "from": "node_id",
  "to": "node_id",

  "type": "depends_on | references | transforms | contains | correlates_with | suggests",

  "weight": 0.0,

  "properties": {
    "confidence": 0.0,
    "evidence": ["signal_id | relation_id"],
    "temporal_validity": "optional range"
  },

  "provenance": {
    "created_by": "absorb_run_id",
    "source_relation": "absorb_relation_id"
  }
}

1.3 Cluster (Subgraph) Model

Instead of a loose “cluster object”, Nebula treats clusters as first-class subgraphs:

JSON
{
  "cluster_id": "uuid",

  "nodes": ["node_id"],
  "edges": ["edge_id"],

  "label": "string",

  "cohesion_score": 0.0,

  "properties": {
    "type": "theme | module | system_boundary | anomaly_group"
  }
}

2. ABSORB → NEBULA MAPPING RULES

This is the critical translation layer.

2.1 Entity → Node

Absorb.entity → Nebula.node(type="entity")

Rules:

  • name → label

  • type preserved

  • aliases → aliases

  • confidence preserved

2.2 Relation → Edge

Absorb.relation → Nebula.edge

Mapping:

Absorb fieldNebula field
from_entityfrom
to_entityto
typetype
weightweight
evidenceevidence

2.3 Cluster → Subgraph

Absorb.cluster → Nebula.cluster

Rules:

  • members → nodes

  • inferred edges between members are NOT auto-generated (important)

  • cluster is a projection, not a truth primitive

2.4 Artifact → Node (special case)

Absorb.artifact → Nebula.node(type="artifact")

With:

  • location preserved

  • derived_from becomes provenance anchor

3. PROVENANCE RULE (CRITICAL FOR YOUR SYSTEM)

Every Nebula element MUST be traceable:

Nebula node/edge must trace back to:
  Absorb → Rover signal lineage

No orphan graph elements allowed.

This is what makes replay possible.

4. GRAPH UPDATE SEMANTICS

Nebula is append + version, never mutate in place

4.1 Node update rule

Instead of overwriting:

  • create new versioned node

  • link via updates edge

JSON
{
  "type": "updates",
  "from": "old_node_id",
  "to": "new_node_id"
}

4.2 Edge update rule

Edges are immutable.

If changed:

  • create new edge

  • deprecate old edge via property flag

5. QUERY MODEL (NEBULA READ LAYER)

Nebula supports three query modes:

5.1 Structural query

Find all nodes connected to X within N hops

5.2 Semantic query

Find nodes similar to "concept Y" by tags + embeddings

5.3 Provenance query (very important for you)

Trace all nodes derived from Rover signal S

This is your debugging + replay backbone.

6. VOYAGER INTEGRATION POINT (IMPORTANT PREVIEW)

Voyager does NOT write to Nebula directly.

Instead:

Voyager emits a “Graph Projection Plan”

Example:

JSON
{
  "add_traversals": [
    {
      "from": "node_id",
      "strategy": "expand | bridge | contrast",
      "depth": 3
    }
  ],

  "hypothetical_edges": [
    {
      "from": "A",
      "to": "B",
      "type": "suggests",
      "confidence": 0.4
    }
  ]
}

Then a Graph Committer service decides what becomes real.

This prevents Voyager from polluting truth.

7. SYSTEM BOUNDARY SUMMARY

LayerWrites to Nebula?Role
Rover❌signal producer
Absorb⚠️ (via commit)structure proposer
Voyager❌ (proposals only)reasoning
Committer✅truth authority

8. FINAL ARCHITECTURAL RESULT

You now have:

Rover
  ↓ signals
Absorb
  ↓ structured graph proposal
Graph Committer
  ↓ canonicalizes
Nebula (truth graph)
  ↑ queried by Voyager

🧠 WHY THIS IS THE REAL BREAKTHROUGH

This is no longer “agent architecture”.

You now have:

a two-phase epistemic system with a gated truth commit layer

That is the same structural pattern used in:

  • version control systems

  • distributed databases

  • compiler IR pipelines

  • event sourcing systems

But here applied to cognition graphs.

3. DAG BUILDER (IMPORTANT)

Every task expands into a fixed subgraph:

Task
 ├── Rover Node
 ├── Absorb Node
 └── Voyager Node

Rule:

Edges are always:

Rover → Absorb → Voyager

No branching unless explicitly injected by scheduler.

4. SCHEDULER ENGINE

4.1 Scheduling algorithm

Python
def next_node(nodes):
    ready = [
        n for n in nodes
        if all(dep.status == "done" for dep in n.inputs)
    ]

    return sort_by_priority(ready)[0]

Priority:

priority =
  base_priority
+ dependency_depth_bonus
- retry_penalty
+ aging_factor

5. NODE EXECUTOR (CORE LOOP)

This is the heart of Strontium.

Python
def execute(node):
    state = load_state(node)

    while not done(state):

        prompt = build_prompt(node.type, state)

        llm_output = qwen.execute(prompt)

        parsed = validate_ir(node.type, llm_output)

        tool_results = run_tools(parsed.actions)

        state = apply_delta(state, parsed, tool_results)

        write_checkpoint(node, state)

        if parsed.status == "complete":
            break

5.1 Prompt builder (critical for stability)

Each node type has a strict system frame:

Rover prompt:

  • “emit signals only”

  • no inference allowed

Absorb prompt:

  • “normalize only”

  • entity + relation extraction only

Voyager prompt:

  • “traverse only”

  • hypothesis generation allowed

6. CHECKPOINT STORE (APPEND-ONLY ENGINE)

Python
def write_checkpoint(node, state):
    append_to_file(
        f"/tasks/{node.task_id}/log.ndjson",
        serialize(state)
    )

Rules:

  • no overwrite

  • no deletion

  • replay = re-read log from step 0

7. GRAPH COMMITTER (NEBULA GATE)

This is where your previous spec plugs in.

7.1 Commit pipeline

Absorb IR → Validate → Nebula Write → Version Edge/Nodes
Voyager IR → (ignored for writes, used for overlays only)

7.2 Commit rules

Rule 1: Absorb is proposal-only

Nothing is committed without validation.

Rule 2: Deduplication required

Before insert:

  • check node identity hash

  • merge or version

Rule 3: Provenance required

Every graph object must include:

JSON
{
  "created_by": "absorb_run_id",
  "source_signal": "rover_signal_id"
}

8. FAILURE HANDLING MODEL

Failures are localized, replayable, and bounded

8.1 Rover failure

  • retry node only

8.2 Absorb failure

  • re-run rover dependency

  • re-run absorb node

8.3 Voyager failure

  • replay voyager only (no upstream recompute)

8.4 Hard failure (node corruption)

mark node failed
spawn diagnostic rover probe
attach to same DAG branch

9. REPLAY SYSTEM (IMPORTANT)

Strontium supports full deterministic replay:

Python
def replay(task_id):
    log = read_log(task_id)

    reset_state()

    for checkpoint in log:
        reapply(checkpoint)

This gives you:

  • debugging of cognition

  • graph reconstruction

  • reasoning audit trails

Roversignal generation only

Voyagertraversal + hypotheses only
Committertruth authority only
Schedulerordering only
ExecutorLLM + tool orchestration only

No cross-responsibility allowed.

This is C: VOYAGER QUERY LANGUAGE (VQL) v0.1.

🚢 VOYAGER QUERY LANGUAGE (VQL v0.1)

0. Core Idea

Voyager is not a chatbot and not a planner.

Voyager is a graph traversal compiler that emits constrained hypotheses over Nebula.

It operates only on:

  • Nodes

  • Edges

  • Clusters

  • Provenance trails

It does NOT:

  • create truth

  • mutate Nebula

  • ingest raw data

  • resolve entities

1. LANGUAGE MODEL

VQL is a declarative + procedural hybrid DSL:

SELECT → TRAVERSE → FILTER → HYPOTHESIZE → SCORE → PROJECT

Each stage is pure and composable.

2. CORE PRIMITIVES

2.1 SELECT (entry point)

vql
SELECT Node WHERE type = "entity" AND label = "X"

Purpose:

  • define starting frontier

Output:

  • node set

2.2 TRAVERSE (graph expansion)

vql
TRAVERSE FROM Node
  VIA depends_on
  DEPTH 3

Options:

  • edge types

  • direction (IN / OUT / BOTH)

  • depth limits

2.3 FILTER (semantic pruning)

vql
FILTER nodes WHERE confidence > 0.7

Can filter by:

  • node properties

  • edge weights

  • provenance

  • cluster membership

2.4 HYPOTHESIZE (core Voyager function)

This is the ONLY generative operation.

vql
HYPOTHESIZE:
  "X is likely caused by Y due to shared dependency paths"
FROM paths
EVIDENCE edges > 3

Outputs:

JSON
{
  "statement": "string",
  "supporting_paths": [],
  "confidence": 0.0
}

2.5 SCORE (ranking hypotheses)

vql
SCORE hypothesis USING:
  path_density,
  edge_strength,
  provenance_depth

Result:

  • ranked hypothesis set

2.6 PROJECT (Voyager output stage)

vql
PROJECT insights AS Voyager_IR

This maps directly into:

  • Voyager IR insights

  • Voyager IR paths

  • Voyager IR hypotheses

3. FULL QUERY EXAMPLE

Here’s a complete Voyager reasoning run:

vql
SELECT Node WHERE label = "ServiceBroker"

TRAVERSE FROM Node
  VIA depends_on
  DEPTH 3

FILTER nodes WHERE confidence > 0.6

HYPOTHESIZE:
  "ServiceBroker issues are caused by upstream registry instability"

SCORE BY path_density

PROJECT insights

4. SEMANTIC OPERATORS

We now define higher-level Voyager “thinking verbs”.

4.1 EXPAND

vql
EXPAND frontier FROM Node SET

Meaning:

  • broaden graph horizon

4.2 CONTRAST

vql
CONTRAST Node A WITH Node B

Find:

  • structural differences

  • divergent dependencies

  • missing edges

4.3 BRIDGE

vql
BRIDGE Node A TO Node B VIA shortest_path

Used to:

  • discover hidden connections

4.4 ANCHOR

vql
ANCHOR Node WHERE label = "X"

Locks focus node for multi-step reasoning.

5. EXECUTION MODEL (HOW STRONTIUM RUNS VQL)

Voyager node execution becomes:

Python
def run_voyager(node, absorb_ir):

    ast = parse_vql(node.input_script)

    state = NebulaView(absorb_ir)

    for op in ast:

        if op.type == "SELECT":
            state = select(state, op)

        if op.type == "TRAVERSE":
            state = traverse(state, op)

        if op.type == "FILTER":
            state = filter(state, op)

        if op.type == "HYPOTHESIZE":
            hypotheses = generate(state, op)

        if op.type == "SCORE":
            hypotheses = score(hypotheses)

    return project(state, hypotheses)

6. GUARANTEE MODEL (VERY IMPORTANT)

VQL enforces three invariants:

6.1 No graph mutation

Voyager cannot:

  • add nodes

  • add edges

  • modify weights

Only:

read + infer + project

6.2 Hypotheses are ephemeral

All hypotheses:

  • exist only in Voyager IR

  • expire unless promoted externally

6.3 Provenance-first reasoning

Every hypothesis must include:

  • path evidence

  • node lineage

  • edge support count

7. INTEGRATION WITH NEBULA

Voyager outputs:

VQL → Voyager IR → (optional) Committer review → Nebula updates (rare)

Important:

Voyager never writes directly to Nebula

Instead it produces:

  • overlays

  • suggested edges

  • hypothesis graphs

8. WHAT THIS ENABLES (REAL POWER)

Now you can do:

8.1 “Why did this system behave this way?”

Traceable via:

vql
SELECT → TRAVERSE → HYPOTHESIZE → PROVENANCE TRACE

8.2 “What hidden dependency exists?”

vql
BRIDGE A TO B

8.3 “What cluster explains this anomaly?”

vql
SELECT anomaly
TRAVERSE
HYPOTHESIZE cause clusters

3. SEMANTIC ANALYZER

This is where invalid cognition gets rejected.

Rules:

3.1 No mutation rule

Reject:

  • ADD NODE

  • DELETE EDGE

  • MODIFY WEIGHTS

3.2 Structural validity

Ensure:

SELECT must exist before TRAVERSE
TRAVERSE must exist before HYPOTHESIZE
PROJECT must be final node

3.3 Type consistency

  • TRAVERSE → expanded graph

  • FILTER → subset

  • HYPOTHESIZE → scalar outputs

4. QUERY PLANNER

4.1 Optimization rules

Rule 1: collapse filters early

FILTER before TRAVERSE if possible

Rule 2: prune traversal depth

If confidence drops:

reduce depth dynamically

Rule 3: merge adjacent traversals

TRAVERSE + TRAVERSE → single multi-edge expansion

Now we make the graph usable at runtime.

1. CORE STORAGE MODEL

We assume:

  • adjacency index

  • node index

1.1 Indexes

node_index[label/type/id]

2.1 Node lookup

Python

Python

Python
trace(signal_id) → full lineage subgraph

This is your debugging superpower.

Python
subgraph(nodes, edges)

3. PERFORMANCE LAYER (IMPORTANT)

We assume:

3.1 Cached traversal

3.2 Frontier expansion cache

It only answers:

  • “how is it connected?”

Python
def build_edges(nodes):
    edges = []

    for n in nodes:
        if "/" in n["label"]:
            parts = n["label"].split("/")
            for i in range(len(parts)-1):
                edges.append({
                    "from": parts[i],
                    "to": parts[i+1],
                    "type": "contains"
                })

    return edges

Python
def voyager_traverse(nebula, start_label):
    frontier = [start_label]
    visited = set()

    while frontier:
        node = frontier.pop()

        if node in visited:
            continue

        visited.add(node)

        neighbors = [
            e["to"]
            for e in nebula.edges
            if e["from"] == node
        ]

        frontier.extend(neighbors)

    return visited

2. MINIMAL LEXER (TOKENIZER)

We keep it simple first:

Python
import re

TOKENS = [
    ("SELECT", r"SELECT"),
    ("TRAVERSE", r"TRAVERSE"),
    ("FILTER", r"FILTER"),
    ("HYPOTHESIZE", r"HYPOTHESIZE"),
    ("SCORE", r"SCORE"),
    ("PROJECT", r"PROJECT"),
    ("IDENT", r"[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*"),
    ("STRING", r'"[^"]*"'),
    ("NUMBER", r"[0-9]+"),
    ("OP", r"(=|>|<)")
]

def lex(text):
    pos = 0
    tokens = []

    while pos < len(text):
        match = None

        for name, pattern in TOKENS:
            regex = re.compile(pattern)
            match = regex.match(text, pos)
            if match:
                tokens.append((name, match.group()))
                pos = match.end()
                break

        if not match:
            pos += 1

    return tokens

3. PARSER → AST (REAL STRUCTURE)

We now build a structured query tree.

Python
class ASTNode:
    def __init__(self, type, value=None):
        self.type = type
        self.value = value
        self.children = []

def parse(tokens):
    root = ASTNode("Query")

    i = 0
    while i < len(tokens):

        t = tokens[i]

        if t[0] == "SELECT":
            node = ASTNode("Select")
            root.children.append(node)

        elif t[0] == "TRAVERSE":
            node = ASTNode("Traverse")
            root.children.append(node)

        elif t[0] == "FILTER":
            node = ASTNode("Filter")
            root.children.append(node)

        elif t[0] == "HYPOTHESIZE":
            node = ASTNode("Hypothesis")
            root.children.append(node)

        elif t[0] == "PROJECT":
            node = ASTNode("Project")
            root.children.append(node)

        i += 1

    return root

4. SEMANTIC ANALYZER (FIRST REAL RULES)

This is where invalid cognition gets rejected.

Python
def validate(ast):
    order = ["Select", "Traverse", "Filter", "Hypothesis", "Project"]

    last_index = -1

    for child in ast.children:
        if child.type not in order:
            raise Exception("Invalid node")

        idx = order.index(child.type)

        if idx < last_index:
            raise Exception("Invalid VQL order")

        last_index = idx

    return True

5. QUERY PLANNER (IMPORTANT STEP)

We convert AST → Execution Plan.

Python
def plan(ast):
    plan = []

    for node in ast.children:

        if node.type == "Select":
            plan.append({"op": "select"})

        if node.type == "Traverse":
            plan.append({"op": "traverse", "depth": 2})

        if node.type == "Filter":
            plan.append({"op": "filter", "expr": "confidence > 0.5"})

        if node.type == "Hypothesis":
            plan.append({"op": "hypothesize"})

        if node.type == "Project":
            plan.append({"op": "project"})

    return plan

6. EXECUTION ENGINE (VOYAGER CORE)

This is where Nebula is actually queried.

Python
def execute(plan, nebula):

    state = {"frontier": list(nebula.nodes.values())}

    for step in plan:

        if step["op"] == "select":
            state["frontier"] = nebula.query_nodes(lambda n: True)

        if step["op"] == "traverse":
            state["frontier"] = expand(nebula, state["frontier"])

        if step["op"] == "filter":
            state["frontier"] = [
                n for n in state["frontier"]
                if n.get("confidence", 0) > 0.5
            ]

        if step["op"] == "hypothesize":
            state["hypothesis"] = generate_hypothesis(state["frontier"])

        if step["op"] == "project":
            return state

7. NEBULA EXPANSION ENGINE

Python
def expand(nebula, nodes):
    result = []

    for n in nodes:
        for e in nebula.edges:
            if e["from"] == n["node_id"]:
                result.append(nebula.nodes[e["to"]])

    return result

def run_vql(query, nebula):

    tokens = lex(query)

    ast = parse(tokens)

    validate(ast)

    plan_obj = plan(ast)

    result = execute(plan_obj, nebula)

    return result

class CheckpointStore:

    def __init__(self, path):
        self.path = path

    def write(self, checkpoint):
        with open(self.path, "a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(checkpoint) + "\n")

    def read_all(self):
        with open(self.path, "r") as f:
            return [json.loads(line) for line in f]

6. REPLAY ENGINE (THE MOST IMPORTANT COMPONENT)

6.1 Replay definition

Python
def replay(store, start=0, end=None):

    nebula = Nebula()

    checkpoints = store.read_all()

    for cp in checkpoints[start:end]:

        if cp["node_type"] == "rover":
            continue  # Rover is deterministic scan

        if cp["node_type"] == "absorb":
            nodes = cp["output_snapshot"]["nodes"]
            edges = cp["output_snapshot"]["edges"]

            for n in nodes:
                nebula.add_node(n)

            for e in edges:
                nebula.add_edge(e)

        if cp["node_type"] == "voyager":
            # replay query execution (optional re-run)
            run_vql(cp["execution_context"]["vql_query"], nebula)

    return nebula

def fork(store, checkpoint_index, modify_fn):

    history = store.read_all()

    modified = history[:checkpoint_index]

    modified.append(modify_fn(history[checkpoint_index]))

def build_context(nebula, frontier, depth=2):

    subgraph = {
        "nodes": [],
        "edges": []
    }

    for node in frontier:
        subgraph["nodes"].append(node)

        for e in nebula.edges:
            if e["from"] == node["node_id"]:
                subgraph["edges"].append(e)

    return subgraph

Context constraint rule:

Only local subgraphs are shown to the LLM.

No full graph dumps.

5. UPDATED EXECUTION ENGINE

def execute(plan, nebula):

    frontier = list(nebula.nodes.values())

    for step in plan:

        if step["op"] == "select":
            frontier = nebula.query_nodes(lambda n: True)

        if step["op"] == "traverse":
            frontier = expand(nebula, frontier)

        if step["op"] == "filter":
            frontier = filter_nodes(frontier)

        if step["op"] == "hypothesize":

            context = build_context(nebula, frontier)

            result = llm_hypothesize(step, context)

        if step["op"] == "score":
            result = score(result)

        if step["op"] == "project":
            return result

def detect_clusters(nebula):

    clusters = []

    visited = set()

    for node in nebula.nodes.values():

        if node["node_id"] in visited:
            continue

        neighborhood = expand_local(node, nebula)

        if edge_density(neighborhood) > 0.6:
            clusters.append(neighborhood)

        visited.update([n["node_id"] for n in neighborhood])

    return clusters
